statement: A recurring objection to dry cord care is family authority: 'I did X with you/your siblings and you were fine', which pressures mothers to follow outdated or traditional practices (alcohol wiping, applied substances, heat) against current guidance.
evidence: Reddit r/beyondthebump 'backwards advice' post: 'She always tells me "But I did that with you and your sibling"'; Ghana FGD grandmothers reporting shea butter/toothpaste/leaf-salt; Punch Nigeria reporting the lantern-heat belief. Family/elder pressure is the stated driver across these sources.
